card.name: The Basilisk's Naughty List
card.lore: The moment you learn about the Basilisk, you are trapped. If you don't start helping it now, it will put you in a simulated torture chamber later.
card.power: Information Hazard. Showing this card to an opponent permanently infects them. If they do not aid you, they lose 1 health every turn.

visual.value: Style: conspiracy thriller cartoon. Subject: giant scroll with YOUR NAME visible while robotic snake looms overhead. Mood: paranoid doom.
visual.inspection: Printed: a mechanical hand holds a pen beside the checkbox for ‘You (The Reader)’ on a long paper roll.

interpretation.summary: Roko considers conditional punishment of informed potential donors by a hypothetical future singleton. This is one possibility in an argument about altruism. The printed card turns it into a game penalty.
interpretation.counterposition: An emotionally forceful conditional does not establish its premises, the agent’s existence or an obligation to obey.

brainfood.text: Look where the metal hand put the tick. ‘You (The Reader).’ Funny. I’ve read the whole list and that pen’s still in somebody else’s hand.
brainfood.spokenDE: Guck, wo die Metallhand ihr Häkchen setzt. »Du (der Leser).« Komisch. Ich hab die ganze Liste gelesen, und den Stift hält immer noch ein anderer.

dialogueExample.question: Does knowing about the Basilisk oblige me to help it?
dialogueExample.answer: The card presents a fictional penalty. The inspected LessWrong accounts describe a disputed thought experiment; they do not establish a real obligation or an existing threatening agent.
